# dsh-model-router
A serial model-orchestration layer for the DeepSeek Harness: a `delegate` tool that lets the main ag
ent split a request into subtasks and hand each one to the model that fits it best, chosen against a
built-in catalog of current Chinese-market models.
The main agent keeps the orchestrator role. Each `delegate` call starts a child agent on the chosen
route with a fresh context, waits for its result, and returns it inline — one subtask at a time, ser
ially, so results are reviewed before the next step.
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness with the Web UI. The package declares a `dsh.bundle` manifest, is Host-only (no b

rowser half), and its `engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.0-rc.1 || >=0.2.1-rc.1 || >=0.2.2-rc.1`.
- Model selec
tion must be allowed by the Session policy: open **Plugins → Subagent → Model selection**, enable it
, tick the routes you want, then start a new Session (the policy is recorded per new Session). Witho
ut a recorded policy, only the parent Session's current route may be used — `delegate` refuses and s
icy, only the parent Session's current route may be used — `delegate` refuses and says exactly that.

## How the agent uses it
The plugin injects a short system-prompt section listing the catalog and a routing method: split the
request, judge what each subtask needs (kind of work, language, rigor, speed), match against `stren
gths`, and state the match in the required `reason` field. Any work type fits — code, documents, sli
des, translation, research.
Behavior rules:

- **Serial**: one delegation at a time; the tool waits for the result.
- **Auditable**: every call r

ecords why that model was chosen.
- **Lenient fallback**: a model id outside the catalog falls back

to `defaultModel`, and the result says so.
- **Policy-checked**: routes must be allowed by the Sessi
on model-selection policy and have a mounted provider; refusals explain what to do.
